subject: Surge POC recap — recommended model slate, ops asks, and QA pack
messages:
From: Jamie Lin <jamie@finlytics.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Ana Torres <ana.torres@finlytics.com>
Date: 2027-05-09T17:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Demo — initial thoughts and clarifying Qs

Thanks for the demo today, Monica. High level — the latency numbers looked good on short queries, and we liked the KV cache demo for our invoice-extraction flows. Two quick asks before we sync with procurement: 1) can you share a prioritized shortlist of three model variants with clear cost/latency/quality tradeoffs (we care about hallucination risk on fiscal language), and 2) a simple prompt set we can run offline to sanity-check regressions before we flip the switch.

Also, can you confirm whether Redwood can set token retention to 0 for the POC; we need assurance for our audit team.

Best,
Jamie
Customer Success Manager, Finlytics

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Jamie Lin <jamie@finlytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ana Torres <ana.torres@finlytics.com>
Date: 2027-05-10T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Demo — initial thoughts and clarifying Qs

Jamie — thanks for the quick note and the context. Short answers up front: yes, we can set token retention to 0 for the POC (we'll include the config and confirmation in the ops playbook), and below is a concise recommended slate plus rationale. I've also attached a small prompt set and the benchmark CSV from our internal micro-bench run against a Finlytics-ish prompt slice.

Recommended shortlist (prioritized):
1) redwood/titan-7b-opt (default) — Best latency and cost profile for short-form extraction tasks; lower token cost, continuous-batching friendly. Expected median latency: ~40–60ms per token on Dedicated NGPUs. Hallucination profile: low-to-moderate on financial language; does well with targeted prompt templates.
2) redwood/atlas-13b-q4_0 — Balanced quality uplift vs cost; better at context reasoning across multi-paragraph invoices and ambiguous field inference. Latency: ~70–110ms per token. Use where recall/precision for extracted fields matters more than raw cost.
3) community/longformer-70b-int8 (fallback) — Highest quality / best for complex cross-document reasoning but materially higher cost and tail latency. Keep as on-demand fallback for batch reconciliation runs.

Tradeoffs notes: cost per token increases roughly 4x from titan-7b-opt to longformer-70b-int8; latency tail risk (95th pct) grows non-linearly with sequence length on the 70b variant. For POC we recommend primarily using titan-7b-opt with the atlas-13b-q4_0 for harder reconciliation flows.

Quality/regression guardrails we propose for the POC:
- Baseline prompt set (attached) + reference outputs — run nightly diff checks against baseline metrics (precision/recall/hallucination rate).
- Canary rollout: route 5% of traffic to atlas-13b-q4_0 for 48 hours before increasing.
- Drift alerting: token-level confidence drop and hallucination heuristics (we'll provide a lightweight detector to run as a post-check).

Ops asks for Finlytics (what we'd need from you):
- Representative sample: 3k anonymized invoice snippets for a 1-week micro-benchmark (CSV or NG sample format).
- Priority flows: a short doc listing the top 5 fields where false positives are costly (e.g., tax ID, total amount, invoice date).
- Access: add ben_carter@redwood.com as procurement contact in HubSpot so we can push an initial commercial outline.

Attachments included: finlytics_benchmarks_v1.csv, finlytics_prompt_set_v2.txt, ops_playbook_checklist.pdf

I'll follow up with a short SOW draft and a proposed schedule for the micro-benchmark. If that sounds good, can we schedule a 30-min checkpoint early next week to lock the sample and field list?

Thanks — Monica
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Monica — this is helpful, thank you. A couple quick clarifying Qs from procurement/security: 1) can you confirm the quantization profile used for atlas-13b-q4_0 in the benchmarks (we need the exact artifact name for our security questionnaire), and 2) what's the expected infra billing model for using titan-7b-opt on Dedicated vs Hosted (ballpark $/1000 tokens)?

Also, we'll pull together the 3k snippet sample by Friday. Can Ben work with our SSO admin on a temporary verification link for RBAC during the POC?

Best,
Ana
Head of IT, Finlytics

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Ana Torres <ana.torres@finlytics.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Jamie Lin <jamie@finlytics.com>
Date: 2027-05-11T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Demo — initial thoughts and clarifying Qs

Ana — quick answers:
- Quantization profile: atlas-13b-q4_0 uses Q4_0 per our model catalog; artifact id: redwood/atlas-13b-q4_0:v1.2. We'll include the model fingerprint and provenance in the SOW pack.
- Pricing (ballpark): titan-7b-opt on Hosted API ~ $0.0025 / 1k tokens; on Dedicated the marginal infra charge is lower once committed (estimated equivalent ~$0.0011 / 1k tokens with a small monthly reserved fee). Exact numbers depend on concurrency and committed qps — I'll have our commercial team produce an indicative pricing sheet once you confirm expected qps.

Operational next steps (I can take these):
- I'll open a HubSpot opportunity and add the procurement contact (Ana) — expected commercial outline by Wed.
- Monica/Karthik: finalize the micro-benchmark prompt list and baseline outputs. Monica, can you share the nightly diff script template (we have a short one in the ops_playbook_checklist.pdf but a runnable snippet would speed things up)?

Closing ask: can we schedule the 30-min checkpoint on Mon 2027-05-16 10:00am PT? If that works for Finlytics I'll lock the invite.

Cheers,
Ben
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
